operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case + spaced identifiers: 'Date of Birth', 'Birth City', 'MPAA Rating', 'Release Date', 'Height (Inches)', 'Character Name', 'Rating Count' — must be double-quoted; column lookup case-insensitive.
Table 'characters' is a SQL keyword-ish name; must be quoted in generated SQL.

actor."Date of Birth" declared DATE but stored as TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD' (storage=['text','null']); ts_fuzzer dispatches to Date|Number(int elements) — first element '1954-02-18' does NOT parse as int, so Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d.
movie."Release Date" declared TEXT (not DATE) storing 'YYYY-MM-DD' — dispatches to String fuzzer, NOT Date; text-stored dates will be fuzzed as random strings.
actor.NetWorth TEXT storing '$250,000,000.00' — String fuzzer; int-like detection fails (has $ and commas), so no +-1 neighbors added.
characters.pay TEXT storing '$5,000,000.00' with null_rate 0.998 (only ~9 non-null rows) — String fuzzer, elements nearly all NULL.
characters.screentime TEXT storing 'H:MM:SS' with null_rate 0.998 — String fuzzer (not Time; declared TEXT), so no HH:MM:SS template.
characters composite PK (MovieID, ActorID) — both members get max_l0=30 cap; sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicate tuples.
characters FKs to movie(MovieID) and actor(ActorID) both exist; parent PKs are single-column INTEGER — FK fill draws from parent's final filtered column.
actor.Gender distinct=2 (Male/Female) but null_rate 0.568; Ethnicity distinct=17 null_rate 0.791 — String fuzzer will produce implausible values, not the 2/17 real ones.
movie.Rating REAL with 48 distinct values in [~5,~8]; Number fuzzer range [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from 'real' (no args) — will emit wild values.
No NOT NULL constraints anywhere (all notnull=0); no CHECK; no UNIQUE indexes — insert failures rare, so TS rows mostly survive.
actor.Biography/Summary are long text (~40 chars truncated samples) — String fuzzer length range [min,max+1] from elements, so ~40-char random strings.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on actor."Date of Birth": template %Y-%m-%d, range from min/max parsed dates (~1921..~2000); p=0.2 means 20% element reuse, 80% fresh uniform dates in range — plausible, low FN.

String fuzzer on movie."Release Date": random a-zA-Z0-9() strings, NOT dates — any query comparing Release Date to a date literal or ordering by it will see garbage; likely FP source (ties/ordering) and FN (no plausible dates).

String fuzzer on Gender/Ethnicity/MPAA Rating/Genre: random strings, not the small real domains — queries filtering 'Gender = Male' or 'MPAA Rating = PG-13' will return 0 rows in generated instances; strong FN driver.

Number fuzzer on Budget/Gross/Runtime/Rating Count: full range [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from type args (INTEGER -> scale 0 -> [-1,1]? actually int family scale default) — implausible magnitudes; queries with numeric thresholds (Budget > 1000000) will match everything or nothing; FN/FP driver.
Number fuzzer on Rating (REAL): scale from 'real' no args -> default; values far from [5,8] real range; queries 'Rating > 7' become meaningless.
Number fuzzer on Height (Inches): real range ~[60,80] but fuzzer emits full int range; 'Height > 70' matches randomly.
String fuzzer on NetWorth/pay: '$...' strings get '%' stripped only; int-like detection fails so no +-1; random strings — money comparisons broken.

Composite PK on characters: sample_fresh_primary_keys keeps first occurrence; FK fill draws from parent final column with replacement, so many duplicate (MovieID,ActorID) pairs get dropped — row count shrinks, ties/duplicates differ from original.

FK fill: characters.MovieID drawn from movie.MovieID final values (634 distinct), ActorID from actor.ActorID (2713) — join cardinality roughly preserved but distribution differs; queries counting characters per movie may see different multiplicities (FP on ties).
String fuzzer contaminate (0.5 prob) adds/removes chars — Title/Name/Character Name get corrupted; LIKE '%Travolta%' queries miss (FN).
p=0.2 default with 0.3 chance whole-instance p=0: when p=0, all columns draw fresh random values (no element reuse) — even more implausible; Date fuzzer with p=0 always-fresh dates.
max_l0 cap (rng*30) on non-PK columns: after ~30 fresh draws, values repeat — creates artificial ties/duplicates that original lacks (FP on DISTINCT/COUNT queries).
